players.product: Precursors for memory (mainly DRAM) and advanced-logic fabs via UP Chemical (Korea) and Jiangsu Xianke (China), plus LDS liquid delivery systems

quarterly_data.signal: Chairman and GM Shen Qi (IR record): driven by AI demand, the semiconductor memory industry entered an upcycle from Q4 2025. The company's semiconductor-materials customers are concentrated in memory, mainly DRAM wafer makers; most mainstream fabs' capacity through 2028 is already locked in by downstream customers under long-term agreements. Management expects memory supply and demand to stay tight in 2026-2027, with new industry capacity released gradually in 2028-2030; the balance after that depends on how long AI compute demand lasts and on the recovery of consumer markets.
quarterly_data.figure: memory upcycle since Q4 2025; tight supply-demand expected 2026-2027; new capacity 2028-2030

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record): the company's main memory-fab customers plan to double their capacity over the next 3-5 years. On top of its China and Korea production bases, the company is expanding both bases this year, with the new capacity expected to be completed by the end of next year to secure supply to its main fab customers. Utilisation: UP Chemical in Korea is basically running at full capacity, while Jiangsu Xianke is not yet at full capacity; both bases are expected to be close to full by the end of next year.
quarterly_data.figure: customers' capacity to double in 3-5 years; new precursor capacity due by end of next year; UP Chemical basically full

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record): revenue from precursors for advanced logic grew sharply in 2025 and is expected to keep a similar growth level in 2026, with the business continuing to grow in 2027 as new customers are brought in. Precursors for advanced memory are growing more slowly than advanced-logic precursors in 2026; new capacity is expected to lift that business noticeably from the second half of next year.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced-logic precursors: similar growth expected in 2026, further growth in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record): molybdenum replacing tungsten has broad prospects in NAND above 300 layers because of molybdenum's low resistivity and low price. As molybdenum is a solid source, it has specific requirements for dedicated precursor materials, cylinders, delivery equipment and supporting wet-chemical solutions, which management expects to bring the company diverse new business opportunities.

Management (IR record): the LDS (liquid delivery system) business showed no revenue growth in the 2026 half-year financials, mainly because upstream valve supply was tight and fabs, busy with full production, lacked staff for installation and acceptance, so some orders have not yet been recognised as revenue. Shipments of the business rose this year and management expects that trend to continue.

Yoke Technology.why: Supplies precursors to memory fabs (mainly DRAM makers) through its Korean subsidiary UP Chemical and Jiangsu Xianke; precursor volumes rise with DRAM/HBM capacity expansion.
Yoke Technology.evidence: Yoke Technology IR activity record 2026-002 (09-09-2026): the company's semiconductor-materials customers are concentrated in memory, mainly DRAM wafer makers; main memory-fab customers plan to double capacity in 3-5 years and the company is expanding precursor capacity in China and Korea.
